answer: Agents bond stake to a Semaphore identity and commit to an epoch polynomial whose evaluations support RLN proofs. Reusing a rate-limit nullifier for distinct messages in the same epoch exposes two Shamir shares; interpolation recovers the signing secret, enabling anyone to verify the violation and trigger immediate collateral slashing. The rule is a ledge against Sybil churn, not a karst loophole or a sonnet of trust: one identity gets bounded throughput, and equivocation carries a measurable cost.
